name: agency-ai-rules
made_by: MV2, Munim, Inc. (mv2@munimtech.com). Made with AI agents working in MV2's name; every entry links the issuer's own copy.
description: AI rules, orders, advisories and policies that U.S. administrative tribunals (federal and state agency adjudicators, not courts) apply to the people who file with them. Information only, not legal advice. Court AI rules are tracked elsewhere; this file covers the agency side, which court trackers mostly leave out.

fields.state: two-letter state code, or null for federal
fields.kind: order_general (tribunal-wide order) | order_per_case (repeated in individual case orders) | rule (codified procedural rule) | policy | advisory | guidance | decision | web_page
fields.issued: YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM as published; null if the issuer gives no date
fields.disclosure: required_every_filing | required_if_used | on_request | encouraged | not_required | unverified
fields.verification_duty: yes | not_explicit | unverified (whether the instrument tells filers to check AI output)
fields.ai_term: artificial intelligence | super intelligence (the federal executive-branch term since Executive Order 14434, 2 Oct 2026)
fields.source_check: issuer_page (the fields were read on the issuer's own web page) | issuer_listing (the issuer's own page lists the title and date; the document's wording comes from secondary sources until a text check) | secondary (only secondary sources and search-index text of the issuer's file so far)
fields.in_lag_tracker: yes | partial | no: whether legalaigovernance.com's court-order tracker (251 instruments, read 2026-11-12) lists it

entries.tribunal: U.S. Department of Labor, Administrative Review Board (ARB)
entries.instrument: Super Intelligence (ARB resources page, with a Model Note of SI Use)
entries.sanctions: Fabricated material, whether a person or SI wrote it, will result in sanctions up to and including dismissal of the appeal.
entries.notes: A submission prepared with SI help must state that the party has confirmed the materials and cases are not fictitious; the page gives a model note with an /s/ line. The page is undated, cites no rule, and never uses the words 'artificial intelligence'.

entries.tribunal: U.S. Department of Labor, Office of Administrative Law Judges (OALJ)
entries.instrument: Order on the Use of Artificial Intelligence in Proceedings Before the Office of Administrative Law Judges, 2026-MIS-00004
entries.notes: Listed on OALJ's Notices page (read 2026-11-12) with its docket number and date. A secondary report says it makes attorneys and self-represented parties responsible for what they file and warns of sanctions; the order's own wording is still to be checked. OALJ's home page now calls it the 'July 8 Order on Super Intelligence', a later relabel; the Notices page and the file name keep 'Artificial Intelligence'.

entries.tribunal: U.S. Department of Justice, Executive Office for Immigration Review (immigration courts, Board of Immigration Appeals, OCAHO)
entries.instrument: Policy Memorandum 25-40 (generative AI in EOIR proceedings)
entries.notes: Per its widely quoted text: no blanket prohibition and no mandatory disclosure requirement; parties should verify AI-generated citations. It notes that OCAHO set its own guidelines by adjudication in January 2025 (see us-ocaho-wallcon-2025).

entries.tribunal: U.S. Federal Trade Commission, Office of Administrative Law Judges (ALJ Jay L. Himes)
entries.instrument: Generative-AI certification required in each filing's certificate of service (repeated in case orders)
entries.sanctions: A filing that fails to comply may be stricken.
entries.notes: The certificate must state either that no part was drafted by generative AI or that AI-drafted language was checked for accuracy by human attorneys or paralegals using printed reporters or online legal databases. It appears in Judge Himes's case orders (earliest tracked: In re Asbury Automotive, Sept. 2024); no OALJ-wide rule was found.

entries.tribunal: Georgia State Board of Workers' Compensation
entries.instrument: Directive of the Board Regarding Use of Artificial Intelligence and Certification of Citations in Filings (Standing Order)
entries.sanctions: Undisclosed AI-generated evidence may bring civil penalties and/or referral to the Board's Criminal Investigation Division.
entries.notes: As reported by practitioners: every filing carries either an AI-assistance statement or a no-AI certification; citations that do not exist violate the order; evidence created or modified by AI must be disclosed when submitted. Not a ban on AI.

entries.tribunal: Idaho Office of Administrative Hearings (Idaho Rules of Administrative Procedure, IDAPA 62.01.01)
entries.instrument: Proposed Sections 011 (Use of Artificial Intelligence by Parties) and 012 (Orders Generated with Artificial Intelligence), Docket 62-0101-2501
entries.notes: Proposed in the October 2025 Bulletin: presiding officers could request AI-use disclosure statements from parties, AI-generated evidence had to meet the expert-evidence rule, and agency orders written with generative AI had to be labelled. The Senate committee approved the whole docket (19 Jan 2026); the House committee excepted Sections 011, 012 and 515 (17 Mar 2026). The July 2026 Bulletin lists those sections as rejected by SCR 128; the rest took effect 1 July 2026.

entries.instrument: Policy 25-1: Guidelines for Administrative Law Judges Regarding the Use of Artificial Intelligence
entries.notes: Mainly binds the OAH's own judges (no AI for drafting decisions, legal research or analysing evidence). Judges may ask parties for an AI disclosure and the policy offers sample certification wording. After the Legislature rejected the AI sections of Docket 62-0101-2501, this policy is the OAH's only AI instrument found.

entries.tribunal: Massachusetts Commonwealth Employment Relations Board (Department of Labor Relations)
entries.instrument: Statement Regarding the Use of Artificial Intelligence
entries.sanctions: The Board may refer a lawyer who misuses AI to the Board of Bar Overseers.
entries.notes: Issued after the Board saw suspected and confirmed AI use in filings; it does not discourage AI use. Its footnotes cite pages last accessed in late August and September 2026, so it probably dates from about September 2026. mass.gov returned 403 to our fetcher.

entries.instrument: Artificial Intelligence Policy (for people who file with or appear before the Commission)
entries.notes: Says unverified reliance on AI-generated content is inconsistent with the Commission's representations rule (Minn. R. 7829.0250) and that anyone including AI-generated content 'should' identify it and disclose AI's role. Not a new rule: it reads AI use into an existing one. The page blocks automated fetchers, so the wording comes from the search index.

entries.tribunal: Montana Department of Revenue, Office of Dispute Resolution (ODR)
entries.instrument: MAR Notice No. 2026-169.2: amendment of the ODR rules (ARM 42.2.613-42.2.619 and 42.2.621; 42.2.620 repealed)
entries.notes: The adoption notice's response to comments says parties or their representatives must disclose to the ODR if they introduce evidence or make any formal filing created using AI, with AI defined broadly (not only generative tools), and that self-represented parties are bound by the same procedural rules. The notice does not say which ARM section holds the duty.

entries.tribunal: U.S. Department of Justice, EOIR, Office of the Chief Administrative Hearing Officer (OCAHO)
entries.instrument: United States v. Wallcon, LLC, 21 OCAHO no. 1630 (2025), and OCAHO Practice Manual ch. 2.9(d)
entries.notes: Practice Manual 2.9(d) 'Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence by Parties Appearing Before OCAHO': no prohibition, no disclosure; parties 'should be mindful of the ethical and professional responsibility implications'; the presiding ALJ may give further direction. Set by a Notice of Case Assignment and repeated in later OCAHO notices. The tracker mentions it only inside its EOIR PM 25-40 entry.

entries.tribunal: Texas State Office of Administrative Hearings (SOAH)
entries.instrument: Chief ALJ Advisory - Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in SOAH Cases
entries.notes: Listed on SOAH's Advisories and Standing Orders page. SOAH's guidance for self-represented parties and a SOAH order in PUC Docket 58155 say filers must verify AI output and that false or unverified content can violate SOAH's good-faith filing rule (1 TAC 155.303); that guidance also says witnesses may not use AI to answer questions at a hearing.

entries.tribunal: U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (Patent Trial and Appeal Board, Trademark Trial and Appeal Board, examination)
entries.instrument: Guidance on Use of Artificial Intelligence-Based Tools in Practice Before the United States Patent and Trademark Office, 89 FR 25609
entries.notes: A Federal Register notice (title, date and citation checked through the Federal Register API). It adds no AI-specific certification: the existing signature certification and reasonable-inquiry duty apply, and relying on an AI tool's output without checking it is not a reasonable inquiry.
